summary: Read a binary tree in which every node stores an integer. Decide whether it obeys the binary-search rule everywhere: the left side of any node holds only strictly smaller integers, the right side holds only strictly larger integers, and both sides themselves obey the same rule. Equal integers fail the test. An empty tree passes. Write yes or no. Comparisons must respect the bounds inherited from every ancestor, not only the parent and child pair.
notes: Compare after trimming trailing newlines. The input is a level-order node count, using a dot for a missing child.
